topic.title: Best-Arm Identification and Pure Exploration
topic.overview: Pure exploration uses sequential measurements to identify the best option or subset, rather than maximize reward while learning. This cluster covers linear and combinatorial bandits, dependent or changing arms, and noisy pairwise comparisons. Algorithms allocate observations adaptively and stop when the evidence supports a decision at a specified confidence level.
topic.whyItMatters: Uniform sampling can waste effort on clearly inferior options while neglecting close competitors. Instance-sensitive lower bounds reveal where information is needed and help separate statistical efficiency from the cost of computing a sampling plan.
topic.evolution: Early representatives study dependent, mortal, and infinitely many arms. Later work develops subset selection and adaptive identification. Recent methods track optimal allocations in linear models and pairwise ranking, while new analyses compare fixed-budget and fixed-confidence settings and extend experimental design to assortment selection.
openQuestions: How can optimal allocations be tracked cheaply when the candidate set is enormous?
What stopping rules remain reliable under model misspecification or changing alternatives?

papers.title: An $\varepsilon$-Best-Arm Identification Algorithm for Fixed-Confidence and Beyond

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Quantile Pure Exploration for Infinite-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper establishes nearly optimal expected sampling and asymptotically optimal fixed-budget guarantees for finding a high-quality action among infinitely many possibilities.

papers.title: Best Arm Identification with Fixed Budget: A Large Deviation Perspective
papers.tldr: A large-deviation framework sharpens adaptive best-arm error guarantees and supports Continuous Rejects, an algorithm that can eliminate arms at any round.

papers.title: Closing the Computational-Statistical Gap in Best Arm Identification for Combinatorial Semi-bandits
papers.tldr: P-FWS combines polynomial computation with asymptotically optimal sampling and polynomial moderate-confidence guarantees for combinatorial best-arm identification.

papers.title: Covariance-adaptive best arm identification
papers.tldr: Algorithms that learn correlations among simultaneously sampled rewards can identify the best option more efficiently at a specified confidence level.

papers.title: Decentralized Randomly Distributed Multi-agent Multi-armed Bandit with Heterogeneous Rewards
papers.tldr: A decentralized bandit framework coordinates clients with different rewards over random networks and provides high-probability regret guarantees.

papers.title: Fast and Regret Optimal Best Arm Identification: Fundamental Limits and Low-Complexity Algorithms
papers.tldr: EOCP combines fast commitment to the best arm with asymptotically optimal regret and optimal or nearly optimal sample complexity.

papers.title: Improving the Knowledge Gradient Algorithm
papers.tldr: iKG improves best-arm identification by choosing measurements that increase the probability of selecting the best option, yielding asymptotic optimality.

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Multi-Armed Bandits Revisited
papers.tldr: The paper establishes cost and regret bounds for bandits with multiple observation fidelities and develops algorithms approaching those bounds.

papers.title: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of a UCB-based Top Two Algorithm
papers.tldr: A UCB-based Top Two algorithm gains an expected sample-complexity guarantee valid at any error level while remaining empirically competitive.

papers.title: Restless Bandits with Average Reward: Breaking the Uniform Global Attractor Assumption
papers.tldr: Simulated single-arm advice yields asymptotically optimal restless-bandit policies without the uniform global attractor assumption.

papers.title: Statistical and Computational Trade-off in Multi-Agent Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: ESM uses mean-field approximations to trade computational cost against regret in multi-agent bandits, asymptotically matching its associated approximated bound.

papers.title: Adversarial Attacks on Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when combinatorial bandits are vulnerable to reward poisoning and shows that an adversary’s knowledge affects attackability.

papers.title: Best Arm Identification for Stochastic Rising Bandits
papers.tldr: Two algorithms identify the best improving option under a fixed budget, with guarantees that require sufficiently many selections.

papers.title: Matroid Semi-Bandits in Sublinear Time
papers.tldr: FasterCUCB reduces sampling costs for common matroids while retaining asymptotically tight gap-dependent regret guarantees.

papers.title: On Interpolating Experts and Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper derives optimal regret and exploration bounds when choosing an option reveals feedback for an entire group of options.

papers.title: On Multi-Armed Bandit with Impatient Arms
papers.tldr: FC-SE and FC-Entry provide guarantees for bandit learning when neglected options leave and new options may arrive.

papers.title: On Universally Optimal Algorithms for A/B Testing
papers.tldr: For fixed-budget A/B testing with Bernoulli rewards, no algorithm can match uniform sampling on every instance and strictly beat it on another.

papers.title: Peeking with PEAK: Sequential, Nonparametric Composite Hypothesis Tests for Means of Multiple Data Streams
papers.tldr: PEAK provides stopping-time-valid tests across multiple data streams, with reported reductions in sample use and computational complexity.

papers.title: Almost Minimax Optimal Best Arm Identification in Piecewise Stationary Linear Bandits
papers.tldr: A parallel identification algorithm finds a near-optimal action in a changing linear bandit environment with sample complexity optimal up to a logarithmic factor.

papers.title: Fixed Confidence Best Arm Identification in the Bayesian Setting
papers.tldr: A successive-elimination variant nearly matches the Bayesian sample lower bound, whereas standard frequentist methods can be arbitrarily suboptimal.

papers.title: Global Rewards in Restless Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper extends restless bandits to joint rewards and develops adaptive policies that outperform precomputed indices in experiments.

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Contextual Linear Bandits and Multi-Armed Bandits with Expert Advice
papers.tldr: The paper establishes matching regret rates for contextual linear bandits and closes a bound gap in a specified expert-advice setting.

papers.title: Optimal Batched Best Arm Identification
papers.tldr: Tri-BBAI and Opt-BBAI identify the best arm with optimal or near-optimal sampling and batching guarantees under their respective regimes.

papers.title: Optimal Multi-Fidelity Best-Arm Identification
papers.tldr: A tight cost lower bound leads to an asymptotically optimal algorithm for identifying the best option using observations of different costs and fidelities.

papers.title: Optimal Top-Two Method for Best Arm Identification and Fluid Analysis
papers.tldr: An allocation-based threshold rule makes top-two best-arm identification asymptotically sample-optimal as the allowed error probability approaches zero.

papers.title: Strategic Multi-Armed Bandit Problems Under Debt-Free Reporting
papers.tldr: An incentive-aware bandit algorithm establishes truthful reporting in equilibrium and bounds regret against the second-highest true mean reward.

papers.title: Constrained Pareto Set Identification with Bandit Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper introduces a near-sample-optimal algorithm for confidently identifying feasible, nondominated options from noisy multi-objective observations.

papers.title: Fixing the Loose Brake: Exponential-Tailed Stopping Time in Best Arm Identification
papers.tldr: The paper constructs best-arm identification algorithms with exponentially decaying stopping-time tails, addressing rare prolonged or never-ending runs.

papers.title: Near Optimal Best Arm Identification for Clustered Bandits
papers.tldr: Two algorithms exploit unknown agent clusters to identify best actions efficiently, with conditional near-optimal sampling guarantees.

papers.title: Near Optimal Non-asymptotic Sample Complexity of 1-Identification
papers.tldr: SEE solves threshold-based bandit identification with finite-sample complexity matching lower bounds up to a polynomial logarithmic factor.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithm for Max-Min Fair Bandit
papers.tldr: Decentralized fair elimination achieves optimal parameter dependence for learning assignments that maximize the worst-off player's reward.

papers.title: The Batch Complexity of Bandit Pure Exploration
papers.tldr: The paper bounds how many batches sample-efficient bandit exploration requires and provides a general algorithm with sample and batch complexity guarantees.

papers.title: Achieving $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/N)$ Optimality Gap in Restless Bandits through Gaussian Approximation
papers.tldr: A Gaussian approximation enables a stochastic-programming policy with a near-1/N optimality gap for degenerate restless bandits under a uniqueness assumption.

papers.title: Balancing Performance and Costs in Best Arm Identification
papers.tldr: DBCARE balances sampling costs against recommendation quality, approaching theoretical risk limits on nearly all problem instances.

papers.title: Constrained Best Arm Identification
papers.tldr: The paper gives sample-optimal methods for identifying the highest-reward option whose average cost satisfies a threshold, allowing dependent rewards and costs.

papers.title: Fast Local Search Algorithms for Clustering with Adaptive Sampling and Bandit Strategies
papers.tldr: Adaptive sampling and bandit-based swap selection accelerate clustering local search while retaining constant-approximation guarantees under the stated conditions.

papers.title: Optimal Estimation of the Best Mean in Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.tldr: A two-phase bandit algorithm estimates the best mean reward with instance-dependent, asymptotically optimal sample complexity.

papers.title: Precise Asymptotics and Refined Regret of Variance-Aware UCB
papers.tldr: Refined analysis of UCB-V reveals unstable sampling limits and optimal variance-aware regret.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Inference for Adaptive Experiments
papers.tldr: Optimistic simulations support inference after adaptive sampling, with asymptotic guarantees and reported confidence-interval width reductions of up to 50%.

papers.title: Box Thirding: Anytime Best Arm Identification under Insufficient Sampling
papers.tldr: Box Thirding uses three-way comparisons to identify strong options when sampling budgets are small or unknown in advance.

papers.title: Exploration-free Algorithms for Multi-group Mean Estimation
papers.tldr: The paper develops exploration-free sampling algorithms with tighter guarantees for estimating every group’s mean under a finite budget.

papers.title: Fixed Budget is No Harder Than Fixed Confidence in Best-Arm Identification up to Logarithmic Factors
papers.tldr: FC2FB converts fixed-confidence best-arm identification algorithms into fixed-budget algorithms with matching sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Optimal Design for Multinomial Logit Model with Applications to Best Assortment Identification
papers.tldr: The paper develops scalable experimental designs for multinomial logit bandits and proves sample-complexity guarantees for identifying the best assortment.

papers.title: Optimal Top-$k$ Identification from Pairwise Comparisons
papers.tldr: An adaptive pairwise-comparison algorithm identifies top-k items with asymptotically optimal sample complexity under latent utility models.
